direction: Capacity-aware ruin scoring: reweight removal_savings by per-node demand fill (demands/capacity) and switch to stagnation-driven diversification when stagnation_ratio is high, targeting the weakest regimes (capacity_level=tight, size=100, demand_dist=uniform).

operations.mechanism: Archive shows all three solvers converge to ~15.74 with a 0.237% SBS-VBS gap, i.e. near-saturated gains from the current ruin score; wins are split 13/11/0 so a structural change in scoring (not just parameter tuning) is needed. KB documents that the L3 template's evolution lever is exactly score_ruin_nodes with deterministic Regret-2 repair and RTR acceptance, and that Shaw-style relatedness/worst removal plus capacity-feasible regret repair is the standard lever for tight-capacity instances. Hence I direct evolution toward a demand-saturation-aware, stagnation-adaptive ruin score while keeping postprocess_mode=none (only allowed mode) and the 500 ms anytime deadline intact.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 the weakest regimes are tight capacity (12 instances, vbs_rel_gap -23.60%), size=100 (-22.47%) and uniform demands (-22.49%), where removal by pure distance savings leaves routes near capacity that Regret-2 cannot refill feasibly. Therefore a hook that scores ruin candidates as removal_savings normalized by route_dists blended with demand saturation (demands/capacity) and that gradually shifts weight toward high-saturation nodes as stagnation_ratio grows will reduce mean objective below the current SBS 15.7435 while keeping solve_ms_mean under 500 ms.
